key_insight: Morpheus, a fully local Greek clinical-text de-identification pipeline, removed 96.59% of annotated identifiers while over-redacting 2.82% of protected clinical-content probes.
clinical_relevance: Local processing could support privacy-preserving reuse of Greek clinical notes without sending identifiable text outside hospital infrastructure.
method: Evaluated 500 LLM-generated Greek discharge summaries across cardiac surgery, cardiology and nephrology.
Two clinicians independently reviewed annotations, with disagreements arbitrated.
Measured identifier removal, clinical-content over-redaction, residual-leak detection and reproducibility.
evidence_signal: On synthetic notes, Morpheus removed 7,666 of 7,937 identifiers (95% CI 96.16–96.96%); two independent runs produced identical verdicts.
watch_item: Real-world validation remains needed: 271 identifier instances survived, mostly institutional identifiers, and the independent egress guard flagged only 2.
paper_title: Morpheus: a fully local, defense-in-depth de-identification engine for Greek clinical text - a benchmark evaluation
